newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Maldives to free Swiss jailed for life for seeds.
newsitem.headline: Maldives to free Swiss jailed for life for seeds.

text.p: A Swiss man jailed for life last year for bringing three marijuana seeds to the Indian Ocean island republic of the Maldives is to be freed and sent home, the Swiss government said on Thursday.
Berne's Foreign Ministry said it had been informed by Maldives authorities that Erich Zimmermann, 25, would be released soon. He has spent nearly 10 months in a prison island.
Swiss President Arnold Koller had urged clemency for Zimmerman, a mason by trade, in a letter last month to the president of the Maldives, Maumoon Abdul Gayoom.

"He (Zimmermann) was sentenced on April 9, 1996, in the capital Male to life imprisonment for possession of 0.5 grams of marijuana seeds under a new anti-drugs law, in very summary proceedings without a lawyer present," the Foreign Ministry said.
"Simultaneously with his release, Erich Zimmermann will be deported from the Maldives and barred from re-entry for life," the Foreign Ministry said.
The three seeds were discovered in Zimmermann's luggage on his arrival in the Maldives from India.
